concerns.text: T008's verification requires performance.json to validate against the ENTIRE model_performance.schema.yaml 'including ... feature_importances', but feature_importances are only populated by T009, which depends on T008. As ordered, T008's stated verification can never pass — an unexecutable check. Scope T008's verification to the sections it produces (test_metrics, bootstrap_ci, paired_ttest) or move the full-schema gate into T009/T010.

T009 instructs to 'append them to features.csv' — an in-place modification of a derived artifact, violating Constitution III ('No data may be modified in place; every transformation MUST produce a new file'). It also makes the re-run of T007–T009 ambiguous (which file do train/split read?) and contradicts T003's 'exactly 12 descriptor columns' check. Write the augmented matrix to a new filename (e.g. features_augmented.csv) with a documented derivation and name it as the input to the re-run.

No task creates or pins the dependency manifest. The constitution requires 'a requirements.txt (or pyproject.toml) at projects/.../code/ pins every Python dependency', and T002 uses `mp_api` while plan.md's dependency list names `requests` — an implementer cannot deterministically build the environment. Add a task producing code/requirements.txt pinning mp_api (and all other imports), verified by installing into a fresh venv and running the entry point.

T009 is too coarse for deterministic execution: it bundles feature-importance extraction, chart generation, performance.json update, the entire FR-012 structural-descriptor augmentation, checksum recomputation, and a full re-run of T007–T009 into one task. Split so the atomizer/implementation can execute the baseline importance path independently of the conditional fallback loop.

'the CSV validates against contracts/raw_dataset.schema.yaml' is ambiguous: that schema describes a single JSON-like object with additionalProperties: false, not a tabular CSV. Specify the validation procedure (e.g. each row validated against the object schema, or a documented tabular mapping) so the check is executable rather than interpretable.
